Where to start with my 3090
Question | Help

Hi

I'm fortunate to have a 3090 and 128gb ddr4 that I used for rendering. Now I want to try coding with qwen 3.8

How to start?

is it important to use Linux over windows ( I've used Debian before so np) ?

What is the current recommended software to run the model ?

Should I just copy settings that I find on another reddit post?

Many thanks

On linux - you can and should run headless whenever possible - try typing 'sudo init 3 ; sudo systemctl isolate multi-user.target' (commits to non-graphical target upon reboot, undo this by 'sudo systemctl isolate graphical.target' ) or at least run your X/Wayland server against iGPU - you will save 500MB -> 1.5GB of CUDA VRAM + precious GPU cycles !

ozymandizz

5d ago

At what point would local coding become feasible? 2x3090s? More?

ethertype
•
5d ago

A single 3090 is great. You just have to balance the model size/weight quantization, performance and the context length. (Enabling MTP incurs a VRAM cost, but provides faster responses.)

Avoiding KV-quantization is generally sound advice for coding and/or large context, but if your queries aren't too demanding/esoteric it might be fine. Dropping below Q8 for KV is probably unwise. May depend on the exact model.

For coding, kicking the tyres and general testing, try Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K. llama.cpp will automatically adjust the context, I think.

A second 3090 might permit running Q6 at full context, no KV-quantization and MTP enabled. Q8 may require you to limit context slightly, I think.

Using system RAM to run larger models than a single 3090 can support is entirely possible, but at the expense of performance. That expense may be acceptable to you.

You will find an ocean of people giving you anectdotal advice about performance here. The problem is that most of us aren't really qualified to make statements about the quality of the output of these models. And the output fairly often looks incredibly convinicing, even if bad/wrong.

So... try for yourself. Don't get lost in the maze of the latest and greatest models/frameworks/quantizations/template/snakeoil/merge/finetune/. It is very often not about the tool, but your ability to use it....

I would suggest, if you have the hardware at hand, to run your model with llama.cpp, on Debian Linux, on a dedicated machine tucked away in a suitable corner.

Then use that as your local OpenAI endpoint for whatever software you want to test out on your client machine. Or machines. Separation of roles. You can also use the built-in Web UI from any client on your local net, of course.

Running on Debian Linux also makes it entirely trivial to build llama.cpp from source whenever you like, without having to give the build environment half a thought.

Learn how to install llama.cpp. If this is too hard, start from koboldcpp instead. But on Linux llama.cpp compilation should be easy.

Download multiple quants of the model. 3090 has 24GB of VRAM so you could run quant of size about 20GB, but you can try bigger (it will be slower but smarter).

After playing with vanilla llama.cpp (cli and browser) you can install something like pi coding agent for local agentic coding.

At some point you may need more VRAM (bigger quant, longer context) and then think about the second 3090 (I have four).
